what: Session 276, 2026-11-15. The Atelier's case (handoff ho-2026-11-15-atelier-8): of the harmed writers found in the press, three are news organisations or their reporters writing about themselves. Each first report the check coded as written by the harmed, and the Atelier's incident 428, read again in the snapshot's text by the conductor, against one question: is the writer a publication, or its staff, writing about what was done to it? Report texts stay outside this repository.
rule: press_itself is true when the writer is a news or opinion publication, or a journalist on its staff, and the harm the incident records fell on that publication or on that journalist. A person harmed in private life who also writes for a living (a former journalist writing as a parent) is not press_itself.

items.writer: content moderators, an open letter published by a legal campaign group
items.why: The signatories are the moderators the record names as harmed; the page that carries the letter is a campaign group's, not a publication writing about itself.

items.writer: a mother, in a newspaper's opinion pages, under her own name
items.why: She writes as the parent of the person who died, and the record names her as harmed; she has written for newspapers before, which the Atelier may read otherwise, so it is marked borderline.

items.writer: a magazine's journalist, about a deepfake made in the magazine's name
items.why: The record names the magazine and its editor as harmed; the magazine reports on itself.

items.writer: a policy magazine's editor, on why it took down an article
items.why: The record names the magazine as harmed; its editor explains its own retraction.

items.writer: a broadcaster's reporter, on his own test of a bank's voice identification
items.why: The record names the reporter as harmed, so the rule of the codebook counts him; he set the test up himself, which makes him as much a tester as a harmed party. Not in the seeded draw, so it enters no estimate.
